note: Track singing-modes (voice-melodies), step 2: Mixolydian over a drone as the major scale with a ♭7, the ♭7 under Do in three keys, then a made-up tune over I ♭VII IV I that lands on the ♭7.

exercise.title: Mixolydian over a drone
exercise.why: Mixolydian is the major scale with one note changed, the ♭7, so the mode is in tune when that one note is: sing it against the drone from above and from below, then land on it over the chord built on it.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. This is the major scale with its 7th note a half step lower: {{b7}}, ringed on the staff. Sing the scale up from the low {{1}} to the next {{1}} and back down, on "oo".
Go slowly past {{b7}}, and listen for it settling against the drone.

Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows on the staff. Sing {{1}}, step down to the {{b7}} under it, and come back to {{1}}, on "ah". Then sing {{5}}, up to {{b7}}, and on up to {{1}}.
Once {{b7}} lands without a slide from both sides, sing it in another key. Use the Key selector below to change the key, then press Start exercise to start the drone there.
When you change the key, the drone moves and {{b7}} is still a whole step under {{1}}.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the band, which plays G, F, C and G again. Make up a short tune from the scale, and sing it on "la". Land on {{b7}} when F comes round: it is the root of that chord.
If you lose your place, hold {{1}} until G comes back.
